headline: Extends a program for Iraqis who worked for the U.S. government in Iraq and temporarily raises a visa processing fee by $1.
what_it_does: The law changes the rules for special immigrant visas for Iraqis who were employed by or on behalf of the U.S. government in Iraq. For the first three months of fiscal year 2014, the number of people eligible is set at the number of pending applications on September 30, 2013, plus 2,000. It sets a December 15, 2013 deadline for applications. It also directs the State Department to add $1 to a fee charged for processing certain nonimmigrant visas and border crossing cards, with the extra money going to the general fund of the Treasury.

who_it_affects.group: Iraqis who worked for or on behalf of the U.S. government in Iraq
who_it_affects.how: They may apply for special immigrant status under the extended program, but only by the December 15, 2013 deadline.

who_it_affects.group: Travelers applying for machine-readable nonimmigrant visas or border crossing cards
who_it_affects.how: They pay an additional $1 processing fee for these documents.
They must increase the visa processing fee by $1 and deposit the collected amounts in the Treasury general fund.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 4, 2013; the application deadline is December 15, 2013, and the eligibility cap applies to the first three months of fiscal year 2014.
